text:
1. Melt Factor Calibration
A temperature-index melt equation was calibrated using SNOTEL SWE change data: M = MF × (T − T₀), where T > T₀
Non-linear least squares estimates MF (melt factor) and T₀ (base temperature).

                     na.strings = c("NA", "", " "))

swe_data <- swe_data %>%
  mutate(
    datetime   = mdy_hm(datetime),
    temp_C     = as.numeric(temp_C),
    change_SWE = as.numeric(change_SWE)

text:
2. Fit Temperature-Index Melt Equation

swe_filtered <- swe_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(change_SWE) & change_SWE != 0 &
         !is.na(temp_C) & temp_C <= 13 & temp_C > 0)

cat(sprintf("Observations for model fitting: %d\n", nrow(swe_filtered)))

Observations for model fitting: 165

melt_model <- tryCatch(
  nls(change_SWE ~ MF * (temp_C - T0),
      data    = swe_filtered,
      start   = list(MF = 2.0, T0 = 0),
      control = nls.control(maxiter = 1000, minFactor = 1e-6)),
  error = function(e) {
    message("NLS did not converge; using linear approximation: ", e$message)
    NULL
  }
)

if (!is.null(melt_model)) {
  mf_estimate <- coef(melt_model)[["MF"]]
  t0_estimate <- coef(melt_model)[["T0"]]
} else {
  lm_model    <- lm(change_SWE ~ temp_C, data = swe_filtered)
  mf_estimate <- coef(lm_model)[["temp_C"]]
  t0_estimate <- -coef(lm_model)[["(Intercept)"]] / mf_estimate
}

mf_estimate <- as.numeric(mf_estimate)
t0_estimate <- as.numeric(t0_estimate)

cat(sprintf("Melt factor (MF): %.4f mm/°C\n", mf_estimate))

Melt factor (MF): -0.0639 mm/°C

cat(sprintf("Base temperature (T0): %.2f °C\n", t0_estimate))

Base temperature (T0): 96.53 °C

cat(sprintf("Melt equation: M = %.4f × (T − %.2f)\n", mf_estimate, t0_estimate))

Melt equation: M = -0.0639 × (T − 96.53)

temp_seq <- seq(t0_estimate, 13, length.out = 100)
fit_line  <- data.frame(temp_C = temp_seq,
                         change_SWE = mf_estimate * (temp_seq - t0_estimate))

ggplot(swe_filtered, aes(x = temp_C, y = change_SWE)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "#4575b4") +
  geom_line(data = fit_line, color = "#d73027", linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Melt Factor Calibration — Temperature-Index Model",
       subtitle = sprintf("M = %.4f × (T − %.2f°C)", mf_estimate, t0_estimate),
       x = "Temperature (°C)", y = "SWE Change (mm)") +
  theme_minimal() +

title: Snowmelt & Runoff: Melt Factor Calibration and Baseflow Separation
text:
3. Baseflow Separation — Lynne-Hollick Digital Filter
The Lynne-Hollick recursive digital filter separates streamflow into baseflow and quickflow components. Three passes improve baseflow isolation.

discharge_data <- read.csv("data/NWIS_discharge.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

discharge_data <- discharge_data %>%
  mutate(date     = mdy(time),
         flow_cfs = as.numeric(value)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(flow_cfs)) %>%
  arrange(date)

lynne_hollick_filter <- function(Q, a = 0.925) {
  bf    <- numeric(length(Q))
  bf[1] <- Q[1]
  for (i in 2:length(Q)) {
    bf[i] <- ((1 - a) / (1 + a)) * Q[i] + (a / (1 + a)) * bf[i - 1]
    bf[i] <- min(bf[i], Q[i])
  }
  bf
}

baseflow <- discharge_data$flow_cfs
for (i in 1:3) {
  baseflow <- lynne_hollick_filter(baseflow)
}

discharge_data$baseflow_cfs   <- baseflow
discharge_data$quickflow_cfs  <- discharge_data$flow_cfs - baseflow

total_volume    <- sum(discharge_data$flow_cfs)    * 86400 / 43559.9
baseflow_volume <- sum(discharge_data$baseflow_cfs) * 86400 / 43559.9

cat("=== BASEFLOW SEPARATION RESULTS ===\n")

=== BASEFLOW SEPARATION RESULTS ===

cat(sprintf("Total flow volume:    %.0f acre-feet\n", total_volume))

Total flow volume:    126054 acre-feet

cat(sprintf("Baseflow volume:      %.0f acre-feet\n", baseflow_volume))

Baseflow volume:      353 acre-feet

cat(sprintf("Baseflow fraction:    %.1f%%\n", baseflow_volume / total_volume * 100))

Baseflow fraction:    0.3%

title: Radiation & Energy Balance: Longwave, Shortwave, and Net Energy
text:
1. Net Longwave Radiation
All-sky emissivity (Brutsaert 1975 modified): ε_all = 0.83 − 0.18 × exp(−0.067 × √ea)

Incoming shortwave computed from solar geometry (Spencer 1971, Spencer 1971 equation of time), attenuated by cloud cover fraction using the Kasten-Young cloudiness transmissivity: HK_in = I_sc × E₀ × cos(Z) × (0.355 + 0.68 × (1 − C_cloud))

               names_to = "variable", values_to = "W_m2")

title: Snow Hydrology — Fall 2025
text:
Course assignments from Snow Hydrology, Fall 2025 at Colorado State University. Analyses use Water Year 2024 data from the Telluride ASOS station (TEX) and Red Mountain Pass SNOTEL site 713.



Topic
Description




Climate Observations
WY2024 temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind, snow depth, SWE, and snow density


Cloud Cover
Cloud cover frequency, precipitation form, and snow crystal morphology


Precipitation Analysis
Undercatch correction, precipitation as snow (3 methods), wind during precipitation


Albedo
Surface albedo simulation and analysis


Snow Interception
Forest canopy interception by tree species (LAI-based)


Blowing Snow
Blowing snow frequency and Pomeroy transport equation


Radiation & Energy Balance
Longwave/shortwave radiation and energy balance


Snowmelt & Runoff
Snowmelt factor calibration and baseflow separation

title: Albedo: Surface Albedo Simulation and Analysis
text:
1. Albedo Simulation
Snow albedo decays exponentially between snowfall events. Fresh snowfall resets albedo to the maximum value; the decay rate is faster during melt conditions (T > 0°C).

alpha_fresh        <- 0.84
alpha_decay_no_melt <- 0.70
alpha_decay_melt   <- 0.50
alpha_soil         <- 0.20
k_no_melt          <- 0.01
k_melt             <- 0.05

asos_data <- ASOS %>%
  mutate(
    snowfall = !is.na(p01i) & p01i > 0 & !is.na(tmpf) & tmpf <= 35,
    albedo   = NA_real_,
    snow_present = FALSE
  )

asos_data$albedo[1]      <- alpha_soil
asos_data$snow_present[1] <- FALSE

for (i in 2:nrow(asos_data)) {
  if (isTRUE(asos_data$snowfall[i])) {
    asos_data$albedo[i]      <- alpha_fresh
    asos_data$snow_present[i] <- TRUE
  } else if (isTRUE(asos_data$snow_present[i - 1])) {
    asos_data$snow_present[i] <- TRUE
    time_diff <- as.numeric(difftime(asos_data$datetime[i],
                                     asos_data$datetime[i - 1], units = "hours"))
    is_melting <- !is.na(asos_data$tmpf[i]) && asos_data$tmpf[i] > 32
    if (is_melting) {
      k         <- k_melt
      alpha_min <- alpha_decay_melt
    } else {
      k         <- k_no_melt
      alpha_min <- alpha_decay_no_melt
    }
    alpha_prev <- asos_data$albedo[i - 1]
    asos_data$albedo[i] <- alpha_min + (alpha_prev - alpha_min) * exp(-k * time_diff)

    if (!is.na(asos_data$tmpf[i]) && asos_data$tmpf[i] > 40) {
      asos_data$snow_present[i] <- FALSE
      asos_data$albedo[i]       <- alpha_soil
    }
  } else {
    asos_data$albedo[i]      <- alpha_soil
    asos_data$snow_present[i] <- FALSE
  }
}

3. Fresh Snow Density — Hedstrom-Pomeroy Equation
The Hedstrom-Pomeroy (1998) equation relates fresh snow density to air temperature: ρ = 67.92 + 51.25 × exp(T / 2.59)

calc_fresh_snow_density <- function(temp_c) {
  density <- 67.92 + 51.25 * exp(temp_c / 2.59)
  pmax(50, pmin(200, density))
}

snow_events <- asos_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(temp_c) & temp_c <= 0 & !is.na(p01m) & p01m > 0) %>%
  mutate(

  rho_max <- 0.5975
  k1      <- 0.0012
  k2      <- 0.0038
  rho_0   <- 0.024
  rho_max * (1 - exp(-k1 * depth_cm - k2 * doy)) + rho_0

cloud_cover_to_fraction <- function(sky_condition) {
  case_when(
    sky_condition == "SKC" | sky_condition == "CLR" ~ 0.0,

    sky_condition == "SCT" ~ 0.375,

    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )

categorize_cloud_cover <- function(sky_condition) {
  case_when(
    sky_condition == "SKC" | sky_condition == "CLR" ~ "Clear",
    sky_condition == "FEW" ~ "Few",
    sky_condition == "SCT" ~ "Scattered",
    sky_condition == "BKN" ~ "Broken",
    sky_condition == "OVC" ~ "Overcast",
    TRUE ~ "Missing"
  )
}

assign_wy_month <- function(datetime) {
  calendar_month <- month(datetime)
  wy_month_num   <- ifelse(calendar_month >= 10, calendar_month - 9, calendar_month + 3)
  factor(wy_month_num, levels = 1:12,
         labels = c("Oct","Nov","Dec","Jan","Feb","Mar",
                    "Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sep"))
}

4. Snow Crystal Morphology (WY2024)

classify_snow_crystal <- function(temp_c, supersaturation) {
  case_when(
    temp_c > 0 ~ "No Snow (Liquid)",
    temp_c >= -5 ~ case_when(
      supersaturation >= 0.15 ~ "Needles",
      supersaturation >= 0.05 ~ "Solid Plates",
      TRUE ~ "Thin Plates"),
    temp_c >= -10 ~ case_when(
      supersaturation >= 0.2  ~ "Needles",
      supersaturation >= 0.1  ~ "Hollow Columns",
      TRUE ~ "Solid Plates"),
    temp_c >= -15 ~ case_when(
      supersaturation >= 0.25 ~ "Stellars",
      supersaturation >= 0.15 ~ "Sectored Plates",
      supersaturation >= 0.1  ~ "Solid Plates",
      TRUE ~ "Thin Plates"),
    temp_c >= -22 ~ case_when(
      supersaturation >= 0.2 ~ "Stellars",
      supersaturation >= 0.1 ~ "Plates",
      TRUE ~ "Columns"),
    TRUE ~ "Columns"
  )
}

estimate_supersaturation <- function(temp_c, rh_percent) {
  case_when(
    is.na(rh_percent)   ~ NA_real_,
    rh_percent >= 95    ~ 0.25,
    rh_percent >= 85    ~ 0.15,
    rh_percent >= 70    ~ 0.08,
    TRUE                ~ 0.03
  )
}

TEMP_ALL_SNOW <- -2
TEMP_ALL_RAIN <-  4

calc_snow_probability <- function(temp_c) {
  temp_mid  <- (TEMP_ALL_SNOW + TEMP_ALL_RAIN) / 2
  temp_range <- TEMP_ALL_RAIN - TEMP_ALL_SNOW
  k          <- 10 / temp_range
  prob_snow  <- 1 / (1 + exp(k * (temp_c - temp_mid)))
  prob_snow  <- ifelse(temp_c <= TEMP_ALL_SNOW, 1.0, prob_snow)
  prob_snow  <- ifelse(temp_c >= TEMP_ALL_RAIN, 0.0, prob_snow)
  ifelse(is.na(temp_c), NA_real_, prob_snow)
}

    method1_snow_mm  = ifelse(method1_is_snow, p01m_corrected, 0),
    method1_rain_mm  = ifelse(!method1_is_snow, p01m_corrected, 0),
    method2_is_snow  = !is.na(dewpoint_c) & dewpoint_c <= 0,
    method2_snow_mm  = ifelse(method2_is_snow, p01m_corrected, 0),
    method2_rain_mm  = ifelse(!method2_is_snow, p01m_corrected, 0),
    snow_probability = calc_snow_probability(temp_c),
    method3_snow_mm  = ifelse(!is.na(snow_probability),
                              p01m_corrected * snow_probability, 0),
    method3_rain_mm  = ifelse(!is.na(snow_probability),
                              p01m_corrected * (1 - snow_probability), 0),
    cumulative_method1 = cumsum(method1_snow_mm),
    cumulative_method2 = cumsum(method2_snow_mm),

title: Snow Interception: Forest Canopy Interception by Tree Species
text:
1. LAI Values and Interception Model
LAI values for three tree species common in the San Juan Mountains (summer/winter):

LAI_quaking_aspen_summer  <- 3.0
LAI_quaking_aspen_winter  <- 0.0
LAI_douglas_fir_summer    <- 6.0
LAI_douglas_fir_winter    <- 5.0
LAI_western_larch_summer  <- 2.0
LAI_western_larch_winter  <- 0.0

get_season <- function(date) {
  ifelse(month(date) >= 6 & month(date) <= 8, "summer", "winter")
}

calculate_interception <- function(precipitation, temperature, lai_summer, lai_winter, valid_date) {
  lai <- ifelse(get_season(valid_date) == "summer", lai_summer, lai_winter)
  ifelse(temperature < 32,
         0.6 * lai * precipitation,
         0.2 * lai * precipitation)
}

ASOS <- ASOS %>%
  mutate(
    p01i_clean = ifelse(is.na(p01i), 0, p01i),
    tmpf_clean = ifelse(is.na(tmpf), 32, tmpf),
    interception_quaking_aspen = mapply(calculate_interception,
      p01i_clean, tmpf_clean, LAI_quaking_aspen_summer, LAI_quaking_aspen_winter, valid),
    interception_douglas_fir = mapply(calculate_interception,
      p01i_clean, tmpf_clean, LAI_douglas_fir_summer, LAI_douglas_fir_winter, valid),
    interception_western_larch = mapply(calculate_interception,
      p01i_clean, tmpf_clean, LAI_western_larch_summer, LAI_western_larch_winter, valid),
    is_storm = p01i_clean > 0
  )

ASOS <- ASOS %>%
  mutate(
    storm_end = ifelse(is_storm, as.numeric(valid), NA_real_),
    storm_end = zoo::na.locf(storm_end, na.rm = FALSE),
    storm_end = as.POSIXct(storm_end, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
    hours_since_storm = as.numeric(difftime(valid, storm_end, units = "hours")),
    interception_quaking_aspen = ifelse(is.na(storm_end) | hours_since_storm > 6,
                                        0, interception_quaking_aspen),
    interception_douglas_fir   = ifelse(is.na(storm_end) | hours_since_storm > 6,
                                        0, interception_douglas_fir),
    interception_western_larch = ifelse(is.na(storm_end) | hours_since_storm > 6,
                                        0, interception_western_larch)
  )
